missed.why: A family P2 did not consider for this function: single 3-state buffers with an active-high OE. One per line, 16 a board. OE comes straight from the enable node, so the gated output buffer needs no enable inverter; the 244s P2 ranks do. SCES224S (revised August 2026, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lvc1g126.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:51:52Z). Output disabled with OE low (section 7). Ioff ±10 µA at VCC 0 V with VI or VO = 5.5 V, which covers A and OE. IOZ 10 µA at VCC 3.6 V with VO = 0 to 5.5 V. Absolute maximum for an output in the high-impedance or power-off state: 6.5 V. So a disabled or unpowered output at 3.6 V sits inside a characterized condition. Section 5.3 gives VO only as 0 to VCC, with no 3-state row. II ±5 µA on A or OE, so 113 kΩ gives 0.57 V, under V_IL 0.8 V; no bus hold is stated. tdis OE to Y: 5.5 ns max. tpd: 4.5 ns max at 3.3 V ± 0.3 V, 30 or 50 pF, −40 to 85 °C. IOH −24 mA and IOL 24 mA at VCC 3 V, so P2's 142 Ω still holds. VCC 1.65 to 5.5 V; TA −40 to 125 °C. Pins: OE 1, A 2, GND 3, Y 4, VCC 5. Load it adds: the enable node drives 16 OE pins, each with its own 10 kΩ pull-down, so 16 × 3.3 V / 10 kΩ = 5.3 mA from R3's OR gate. P5 or the re-rank checks that against the OR gate. Open-drain inverter, a family P2 did not consider. Each active-low OE pin already carries its own 10 kΩ pull-up. The output only pulls OE low, to enable. With the inverter unpowered or its input low, OE is released and the pull-ups read disabled. SCES295AB (revised October 2025, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lvc1g06.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:54:35Z). Ioff ±10 µA at VCC 0 V with VI or VO = 5.5 V. II ±1 µA. VO recommended 0 to 5.5 V. VOL 0.4 V at IOL 16 mA; P2's load is 0.33 mA a pin. tpd 4 ns max at 3.3 V ± 0.3 V (−40 to 85 °C) and 4.5 ns (to 125 °C). tPLZ and tPZL equal tpd (note E). TA −40 to 125 °C. DBV pins: NC 1, A 2, GND 3, Y 4, VCC 5, the same as rank 1 SN74LVC1G04DBVR. Disable time (derived, not measured): OE rises through its 10 kΩ pull-up. The pin capacitance is not stated for the 244s here; at 10 pF the time to 2.0 V is about 0.94 × 10 kΩ × 10 pF = 94 ns. Add the 244's disable time; the sum stays inside the 1 µs budget. exclusions_not_holding.part: 74CBTLV3126DS,118 (C546436), Nexperia; dropped under multiprotocol port path, UART socket path and both reply path through the gate entries
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: fails connector level: 74CBTLV3126 Rev. 7 recommends VSW 0 to VCC in enable and disable mode, under the 3.6 V a KISS line brings with VCC at 3.201 to 3.399 V
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The requirement value is 'a 3.6 V level from the device passes the enabled element without damage'. Damage is set by the limiting values, not the recommended range. 74CBTLV3126 Rev. 7, 11 April 2024 (https://assets.nexperia.com/documents/data-sheet/74CBTLV3126.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:51:50Z), Table 4: VSW −0.5 V to VCC + 0.5 V in enable and disable mode. That is 3.701 V at VCC 3.201 V and 3.899 V at 3.399 V, both above 3.6 V. Note [2]: the rating may be exceeded if the clamping-current ratings are observed. Unpowered, Table 6 gives IOFF ±10 µA (−40 to 85 °C) and ±50 µA (to 125 °C) at VCC 0 V with VI or VO = 0 to 3.6 V. That is the same condition P2 accepts from SN74CBTLV3126 for I_off on the enable. P2's rank 1 passes only on its absolute maximum: SCDS038N (revised July 2026, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74cbtlv3126.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:52:49Z) gives VI −0.5 to 4.6 V in 5.1, and 5.3 has no switch-voltage row. So the drop applies a stricter test than the one the rank-1 part passes. The margin is 0.10 V at VCC 3.201 V. Operation above the recommended VSW is not characterized; the re-rank rules on whether 'passes' needs it. JLCPCB (vendors.py jlcpcb C546436, 2026-09-29T00:51:14Z): stockCount 3983, canPresaleNumber 3983. The DS package is SSOP16, not the PW footprint of SN74CBTLV3126PWR, so it is a separate candidate and not a drop-in alternate.

The only open point is the recommended 0 to VCC with the switch on, the same point as for the Nexperia part above. exclusions_not_holding.part: SN74LV4T125PWR (C90755), Texas Instruments; dropped under gated output buffer
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: fails connector voltage tolerated: SCLS749C 6.3 recommends VO in the H-Z state at 0 to VCC, under 3.6 V
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The requirement value reads 'at least 3.6 V at an output while disabled (VCC 3.3 V) or unpowered (VCC 0 V), without damage'. SCLS749C (revised June 2022, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lv4t125.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:51:51Z), section 6.1: 'Voltage range applied to any output in the high-impedance or power-off state' is −0.5 to 4.6 V. So 3.6 V disabled or unpowered is within the rating that bounds damage. Ioff is 5 µA at VCC 0 V with VO or VI = 0 to 5.5 V. The recommended 0 to VCC in the H-Z state means leakage above VCC is not characterized, not that the part is damaged. Section 6.1 also lists IOK ±50 mA for VO > VCC, which points to an output clamp to VCC. The current it passes at 3.6 V against VCC 3.201 V is not stated. The drop reason does not follow from the requirement as written; the re-rank rules on the clamp. Other values it would still have to meet: IOH −8 mA at VCC 3.3 V (6.3), which moves P2's short-circuit resistor from 142 Ω to 3.4 V / 8 mA = 425 Ω, and 4 parts a board with active-low OE through the enable inverter. JLCPCB (vendors.py jlcpcb C90755, 2026-09-29T01:01:10Z): stockCount 7168, canPresaleNumber 7121.
